subject: mixing multivariate shrinkage model with a univariate level regression.

messages.author: 21b39e2b255e81ed
messages.subject: mixing multivariate shrinkage model with a univariate level regression.
parts:
I am using the shrinkage model used "projection predictive input variable selection using Stan+R" ; with a difference that it is combined, with a multi-level univariate regression;

functions {
// square root of a vector (elementwise)
vector sqrt_vec(vector x) {
vector[dims(x)[1]] res;

for (m in 1:dims(x)[1]){
res[m] = sqrt(x[m]);
}
return res;
}
}


data {
     int<lower=1> Nobs; // number of subjects
     int<lower=1> p; // number of taxa
     int<lower=1> Ngroup; // number of taxa
     int<lower=1> group_id[Nobs]; //indicator variable for each observation
     vector[Nobs] y; //body weight
     vector[Nobs] x_pt; // previous bw matrix
     matrix[Nobs, p] X; // abundance matrix
     // matrix[Npred, p] X_pred; //test
     }

parameters {
  vector[Ngroup] alpha; // slop for each group
  vector<lower=0>[Ngroup] sigma; //error scale
  
  // auxiliary variables for the variance parameters
vector[p] z;
real<lower=0> r1_global;
real<lower=0> r2_global;
vector<lower=0>[p] r1_local;
vector<lower=0>[p] r2_local;
}

transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> tau;
vector<lower=0>[p] lambda;
  vector[p] beta;
tau = r1_global * sqrt(r2_global);
lambda = r1_local .* sqrt_vec(r2_local);
beta = z .* lambda*tau;
}

model {
  y ~ normal(x_pt .* alpha[group_id] + X * beta, sigma[group_id]); //recommended to be log normal
  z ~ normal(0, 1);
r1_local ~ normal(0.0, 1.0);
r2_local ~ inv_gamma(0.5*3.0, 0.5*3.0);
// half cauchy for tau
r1_global ~ normal(0.0, 1.0);
r2_global ~ inv_gamma(0.5, 0.5);
}

generated quantities {
  vector[Nobs] log_lik;
  for(i in 1:Nobs)
  {
    log_lik[i] = normal_log(y[i], x_pt .* alpha[group_id] + X * beta, sigma[group_id]); #normal_lpdf
  }

}
I wonder basically, why my Pareto K estimates are greater than 1, which led loo return NA values and WAIC are so big.

1) Is it because my model is ill-defined, 
2) Is it because my model has so many variables and does not converge ?
3) is there any other shrinkage approach I can use
